PMAY-Urban targets slum dwellers, economically weaker sections (EWS), low-income groups (LIG), and middle-income groups (MIG). The scheme provides interest subsidy on home loans through the Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS). EWS beneficiaries can receive subsidies up to Rs. 2.67 lakh on loans up to Rs. 6 lakh. Beneficiaries must not own a pucca house anywhere in India and must apply with the Aadhaar number. PMAY-Gramin (rural) provides financial assistance to homeless and houseless households in rural areas identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census. A beneficiary receives Rs. 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs. 1.30 lakh in hilly and difficult areas to construct a house with basic amenities. Application can be made through the PMAY portal, Common Service Centres, or bank branches. The scheme prioritizes SC/ST, minorities, and women. Houses must have a toilet, LPG connection, electricity connection, and drinking water access to promote dignity and quality of life.

fields.title: Your Right to Information
fields.summary: How to use the RTI Act to access government information.
fields.content: The Right to Information Act 2005 is one of India's most powerful transparency tools, giving citizens the right to request information from any public authority. Any citizen can file an RTI application with the Public Information Officer (PIO) of any central or state government department or agency. The fee for filing an RTI is just Rs. 10 for central government departments, though some states may charge differently. Applicants from below-poverty-line backgrounds are exempt from fees. The PIO must respond within 30 days, or 48 hours if the information concerns life or liberty. If the response is unsatisfactory or not received, appeal to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days. A second appeal can be made to the Central Information Commission or State Information Commission. RTI can be used to track status of applications, check public works quality, access government records, and expose corruption. Write your RTI application clearly stating the specific information needed. Attach proof of fee payment. RTI cannot be used to get personal information of others or information that would harm national security. The Act has been used by citizens to expose corruption, check ration card status, track road construction, and verify school records.

fields.title: Employment Schemes: MGNREGA
fields.summary: Understanding India's rural employment guarantee program.
fields.content: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) is one of the world's largest public works programs, guaranteeing 100 days of wage employment per year to rural households whose adult members are willing to do unskilled manual work. The program was enacted in 2005 and covers all rural districts of India. Any rural adult can apply for work at the local gram panchayat. Work must be provided within 15 days of application, and if not, an unemployment allowance must be paid. MGNREGA wages vary by state, ranging from approximately Rs. 200-350 per day. Work is focused on natural resource management, water conservation, land development, and rural infrastructure. The program is demand-driven, meaning workers approach the panchayat for work rather than the government assigning it. Workers must be paid through bank accounts or post offices to prevent wage theft. The program has been instrumental in empowering rural women who constitute nearly 55% of workers. Job cards issued to registered households serve as official documents for accessing the scheme. The scheme has reduced distress migration, provided drought relief, and created durable community assets.

fields.title: How Panchayati Raj Works
fields.summary: Understanding local self-governance in rural India.
fields.content: The Panchayati Raj system is India's system of local self-governance at the village level, constitutionally mandated by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment of 1992. The system has three tiers: the Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level. The Gram Sabha, consisting of all registered voters in a village, is the foundation of democratic governance at the grassroots level. Gram Sabhas meet at least twice a year to discuss development plans, review accounts, and elect representatives. Gram Panchayats are responsible for implementing government schemes, maintaining local infrastructure, collecting local taxes, and maintaining records. One-third of seats in Panchayati Raj institutions are reserved for women, and seats are also reserved for SC and ST communities. The Panchayat is responsible for local roads, drainage, drinking water, street lighting, sanitation, and public health. Citizens can raise issues directly at Gram Sabha meetings. Social audits allow communities to examine how funds have been spent on government projects. Strengthening local governance through active citizen participation makes democracy more responsive to community needs.

fields.title: Consumer Rights and Protection
fields.summary: Know your rights as a consumer in India.
fields.content: Consumers in India are protected by the Consumer Protection Act 2019, which replaced the earlier 1986 act with stronger provisions. Every consumer has six fundamental rights: the right to safety, the right to be informed, the right to choose, the right to be heard, the right to seek redressal, and the right to consumer education. The Consumer Protection Act covers goods, services, and e-commerce. If you receive a defective product or deficient service, you can file a complaint with consumer courts. District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions handle claims up to Rs. 1 crore. State Commissions handle claims between Rs. 1-10 crore, and the National Commission handles claims above Rs. 10 crore. The National Consumer Helpline (1800-11-4000) provides free guidance on consumer complaints. The e-Daakhil portal allows online filing of consumer complaints. Always keep receipts, warranties, and records of transactions for potential complaints. Common consumer issues include overcharging, selling expired products, misleading advertisements, and defective products. E-commerce consumers have specific protections including right to return products and refund policies. Consumer awareness is the best protection: know what you are buying, from whom, and on what terms.

fields.title: Digital India Initiatives
fields.summary: How government is using technology to improve citizens' lives.
fields.content: Digital India is a flagship government program launched in 2015 to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. The program has three core components: digital infrastructure as a utility for every citizen, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens. DigiLocker provides a cloud-based platform for citizens to store and share digital documents, reducing the need to carry physical documents. Aarogya Setu and CoWIN apps demonstrated the power of digital health infrastructure during the COVID-19 pandemic. e-Governance platforms allow citizens to access government services online without visiting offices. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has revolutionized digital payments in India, with billions of transactions monthly. The PM-WANI initiative enables public Wi-Fi hotspot network expansion across India. Common Service Centres (CSCs) provide digital services in rural areas where internet access is limited. National Digital Literacy Mission aims to make one member of every household digitally literate. UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) provides access to over 1,200 government services on a single app. Digital India has improved transparency, reduced corruption, and made government services more accessible to ordinary citizens.

fields.title: Banking and Financial Inclusion
fields.summary: Government schemes to bring banking services to everyone.
fields.content: Financial inclusion ensures that individuals and businesses have access to affordable financial products and services. Jan Dhan Yojana, launched in 2014, opened over 50 crore bank accounts for previously unbanked Indians, many in rural and poor urban areas. Jan Dhan accounts come with a debit card, accident insurance of Rs. 2 lakh, and overdraft facility up to Rs. 10,000 after satisfactory account operation. The India Post Payments Bank brings banking services to every post office in India. The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana offers life insurance of Rs. 2 lakh for a premium of just Rs. 436 per year. The Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana offers accidental insurance of Rs. 2 lakh for Rs. 20 per year. The Atal Pension Yojana provides a guaranteed minimum monthly pension of Rs. 1,000-5,000 for workers in the unorganized sector. Banking Correspondent agents bring banking services to villages without bank branches. Mobile banking apps allow account management without visiting branches. Understanding basic banking: keeping money in savings accounts earns interest and is safer than keeping cash at home. Bank Fixed Deposits offer higher interest than savings accounts for medium-term savings.

fields.title: Environment Protection Laws
fields.summary: Laws that protect India's natural environment.
fields.content: India has a comprehensive framework of environmental laws that protect air, water, forests, and wildlife. The Environment Protection Act 1986 is the umbrella legislation empowering the government to take measures for environmental protection. The Air Prevention and Control of Pollution Act 1981 regulates air quality standards and controls emissions from industries and vehicles. The Water Prevention and Control of Pollution Act 1974 prohibits discharge of pollutants into water bodies and established Pollution Control Boards. The Forest Conservation Act 1980 regulates the diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes, requiring central government approval. The Wildlife Protection Act 1972 protects wild animals and plants, establishing protected areas. The National Green Tribunal (NGT), established in 2010, is a specialized court for environmental cases, allowing citizens to file complaints about environmental damage. Citizens can file complaints about illegal construction, industrial pollution, waste dumping, and encroachment of natural areas. Environmental Impact Assessments are required before major development projects. The Clean Air Campaign and National Clean Air Programme aim to reduce particulate pollution in polluted cities. Environmental compliance is not just a government responsibility but a citizen duty.

fields.title: Labour Rights in India
fields.summary: Understanding the rights of workers in India.
fields.content: Workers in India are protected by a comprehensive framework of labor laws that regulate employment conditions, wages, and workplace safety. The four Labour Codes enacted in 2019-2020 consolidated 29 central labor laws: the Code on Wages, Industrial Relations Code, Social Security Code, and Occupational Safety Code. The Code on Wages guarantees a minimum wage for all workers and prohibits gender-based wage discrimination. The Employees Provident Fund provides retirement savings through mandatory contributions from both employee and employer. Employees State Insurance provides health insurance and sick pay to workers below a certain wage threshold. The Gratuity Act entitles employees to a gratuity payment of 15 days wages for every year of service after completing 5 years. Workers have the right to a safe workplace: employers must provide protective equipment and maintain safe working conditions. Maternity leave of 26 weeks is mandated for women employed in establishments with 10 or more employees. Child labor in hazardous industries is prohibited for children below 14 years. Workers can organize into trade unions and engage in collective bargaining. The Labour Department in each state handles complaints about violations of labor laws.

fields.title: Disaster Management in India
fields.summary: How India prepares for and responds to natural disasters.
fields.content: India is vulnerable to a wide range of natural disasters including floods, droughts, cyclones, earthquakes, and landslides. The Disaster Management Act 2005 established a comprehensive institutional framework for disaster risk reduction and response. The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) coordinates disaster management at the national level, while State Disaster Management Authorities coordinate at the state level. The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is a specialized force of 16 battalions trained for disaster rescue and relief operations. The Incident Command System organizes disaster response through a clear chain of command. Early warning systems provide advance notice of cyclones, floods, and tsunamis, enabling timely evacuation. Community-based disaster preparedness trains local communities in first response and evacuation. The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, to which India is committed, focuses on preventing new risks and reducing existing risks. Citizens should know their local disaster risks, nearest evacuation route, and emergency contacts. Keeping an emergency kit with water, food, medicines, documents, and a torch is basic preparedness. Mock drills and community awareness campaigns help prepare communities for disaster response.

fields.title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
fields.summary: A beginner-friendly introduction to AI and how it affects your life.
fields.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the ability of machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence. AI systems learn from data, identify patterns and make decisions. Machine Learning is a branch of AI where computers learn from examples without being explicitly programmed. Deep Learning uses neural networks inspired by the human brain to process complex data like images, sound, and text. AI is already part of your daily life: when YouTube recommends videos, when Gmail filters spam, when Google Maps predicts traffic, or when Spotify suggests songs. Natural Language Processing allows computers to understand and generate human language, powering chatbots and translation services. Computer Vision enables machines to interpret visual information, used in facial recognition, self-driving cars, and medical imaging. AI helps doctors detect diseases earlier, helps scientists discover new medicines and helps farmers improve crop yields. Generative AI like ChatGPT and DALL-E can create text, images, code, and music from simple prompts. While AI brings great benefits, it also raises concerns about job displacement, bias, privacy, and autonomous weapons that society must address thoughtfully.

fields.title: How Smartphones Work
fields.summary: The engineering marvel that fits in your pocket.
fields.content: A modern smartphone is one of the most complex devices ever created, packing technologies that would have filled an entire room 50 years ago. The processor, or System on Chip (SoC), is the brain of the phone, handling all computations. Apple's A-series and Qualcomm's Snapdragon chips contain billions of transistors etched on chips smaller than a fingernail. RAM (Random Access Memory) stores data being actively used, while storage (eMMC or UFS) holds apps, photos, and files. The display, often OLED, creates images by controlling millions of tiny lights with electric current. Touchscreens detect the electrical capacitance of your finger to determine where you are touching. The camera system uses computational photography, combining optics with AI algorithms, to produce images far beyond what the lens alone could capture. 4G and 5G radios enable wireless internet connectivity. GPS receivers determine location using satellite signals. The battery converts chemical energy to electrical energy through lithium-ion technology. Sensors including accelerometer, gyroscope, barometer, and proximity sensor enable features from auto-rotation to step counting. All these components communicate through a sophisticated circuit board and are powered by a surprisingly small software stack.

fields.title: The Science of Climate Change
fields.summary: The physics and chemistry behind global warming.
fields.content: Understanding climate change requires understanding the greenhouse effect, a natural process that makes Earth habitable. The Sun's energy reaches Earth as visible light, passes through the atmosphere, and warms the surface. The warmed surface emits heat as infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases like CO2, methane, and water vapor absorb this outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit it in all directions, keeping Earth warm. This natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth about 33 degrees Celsius warmer than it would otherwise be. Human activities, primarily burning fossil fuels and deforestation, have increased atmospheric CO2 concentration from about 280 parts per million (ppm) before industrialization to over 420 ppm today. This enhanced greenhouse effect is causing additional warming. The Keeling Curve, measured continuously at Mauna Loa since 1958, shows the steady rise of atmospheric CO2. Ice cores from Antarctica and Greenland reveal past climate records going back 800,000 years, showing the correlation between CO2 levels and temperature. Positive feedback loops amplify warming: melting sea ice reduces Earth's reflectivity, and thawing permafrost releases stored methane. The science of climate change is among the most thoroughly tested and verified in all of science.

fields.title: Introduction to Coding
fields.summary: Your first steps into the world of programming.
fields.content: Programming is giving instructions to a computer in a language it can understand to perform specific tasks. Programming languages are formal languages with strict rules for writing instructions. Python is one of the most beginner-friendly languages and is also used by professional data scientists, AI researchers, and web developers. A variable stores data: name = Priya stores the text Priya with the label name. Conditional statements let programs make decisions: if score > 50: print Passed. Loops repeat actions: for each student in class list: calculate average. Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks, keeping code organized. Programs follow sequential execution by default, processing instructions from top to bottom. Data structures like lists, dictionaries, and tuples organize collections of data. Object-Oriented Programming organizes code around objects that combine data and functions. Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors in code. Reading error messages carefully almost always reveals what went wrong. Version control with Git tracks changes to code over time, allowing collaboration and recovery from mistakes. The best way to learn programming is to build small projects that solve real problems you care about.

fields.title: Space Exploration and Missions
fields.summary: Humanity's journey beyond Earth and what we have discovered.
fields.content: Space exploration has transformed our understanding of the universe and our place in it. The Space Age began in 1957 when the Soviet Union launched Sputnik, the first artificial satellite. Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space in 1961. The Apollo 11 mission landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon in 1969, one of humanity's greatest achievements. Unmanned probes have visited every planet in the solar system. The Voyager 1 spacecraft, launched in 1977, has crossed into interstellar space. The Mars rovers, including Curiosity and Perseverance, have explored the Martian surface in extraordinary detail. The Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, has revolutionized astronomy with stunning images of distant galaxies. The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, can see the universe's first galaxies. India's space program ISRO has achieved remarkable milestones: Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the Moon's south pole in 2023, making India the fourth country to land on the Moon and the first to land near the pole. Mangalyaan reached Mars on its first attempt. Private companies like SpaceX are making space access more affordable and driving renewed lunar and Mars ambitions.

fields.title: How the Human Body Works
fields.summary: The amazing systems that keep you alive and functioning.
fields.content: The human body is an extraordinarily complex biological machine consisting of approximately 37 trillion cells working in coordination. Major organ systems include the skeletal, muscular, nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, endocrine, reproductive, immune, and urinary systems. The cardiovascular system circulates blood throughout the body. The heart beats about 100,000 times per day, pumping 7,500 liters of blood. Blood vessels include arteries (carrying oxygenated blood from the heart), veins (returning deoxygenated blood to the heart), and capillaries (the tiny vessels where gas and nutrient exchange occurs). The respiratory system brings oxygen into the body and expels carbon dioxide: we breathe about 20,000 times per day. The digestive system breaks food down into nutrients: digestion begins in the mouth and continues through the stomach and small intestine, where most nutrients are absorbed. The nervous system, including the brain and spinal cord, coordinates all body activities through electrical and chemical signals. The endocrine system uses hormones as chemical messengers to regulate metabolism, growth, reproduction, and mood. The immune system defends against pathogens through multiple layers of physical barriers, innate immunity, and adaptive immunity.

fields.title: Renewable Energy Explained
fields.summary: How solar, wind, and other clean energy sources work.
fields.content: Renewable energy comes from sources that naturally replenish on a human timescale, unlike fossil fuels which take millions of years to form. Solar energy converts sunlight directly into electricity using photovoltaic cells made of semiconductor materials, typically silicon. When photons from sunlight strike the silicon, they knock electrons loose, creating an electrical current. Solar thermal systems use mirrors or lenses to concentrate sunlight to generate heat for electricity generation. Wind energy uses the kinetic energy of moving air to spin turbines connected to generators. Wind is created by temperature differences across the Earth's surface. Hydroelectric power generates electricity from falling water, currently providing about 16% of global electricity. India has massive renewable energy ambitions: 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. The Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan is one of the world's largest solar parks. Battery storage technology, particularly lithium-ion batteries, is critical for storing renewable energy to supply power when the sun is not shining and wind is not blowing. Green hydrogen, produced using renewable electricity to split water, is emerging as a clean fuel for heavy industry and transport. The cost of solar and wind energy has fallen over 90% in the last decade, making them the cheapest sources of new electricity generation in most of the world.

fields.title: Genetics and DNA
fields.summary: How your genes shape who you are.
fields.content: Genetics is the study of genes, heredity, and genetic variation in living organisms. DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the molecule that carries genetic information. The structure of DNA was discovered by James Watson, Francis Crick, Rosalind Franklin, and Maurice Wilkins in 1953. DNA has a double helix structure, like a twisted ladder, with four chemical bases: Adenine, Thymine, Guanine, and Cytosine. The sequence of these bases encodes genetic information, like letters forming words and sentences. A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a specific protein. The human genome contains approximately 3 billion base pairs and about 20,000 genes. Genes are organized on 23 pairs of chromosomes in human cells. Heredity is the transmission of genetic information from parents to offspring. You inherit one copy of each chromosome pair from each parent. Mutations are changes in DNA sequence that can be harmful, neutral, or occasionally beneficial. Natural selection acts on heritable variation, driving evolution. The Human Genome Project, completed in 2003, mapped the entire human genetic sequence. Genetic testing can reveal disease risk, ancestry, and guide personalized medicine. CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing technology allows precise modification of DNA, with enormous potential for treating genetic diseases.

fields.title: The Internet of Things (IoT)
fields.summary: How everyday objects are becoming connected and smart.
fields.content: The Internet of Things (IoT) refers to the network of physical devices, vehicles, appliances, and other objects embedded with sensors, software, and connectivity that enables them to collect and exchange data. The concept has transformed from science fiction to everyday reality: your smartphone, smart TV, fitness tracker, and smart speakers are all IoT devices. Industrial IoT applies connected devices to manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, and infrastructure. Smart homes use IoT devices for automated lighting, temperature control, security, and energy management. Wearable health monitors continuously track heart rate, blood oxygen, sleep patterns, and activity levels. Agricultural IoT sensors monitor soil moisture, temperature, and crop health to optimize irrigation and fertilizer use. Smart cities use IoT for traffic management, waste collection optimization, and environmental monitoring. By 2025, an estimated 75 billion IoT devices will be connected worldwide. Each connected device can be a potential security vulnerability: strong passwords, regular firmware updates, and network segmentation are important security practices. Data privacy is a significant concern as IoT devices continuously collect personal and behavioral data. Edge computing processes data near where it is collected rather than sending everything to distant cloud servers, reducing latency and bandwidth requirements.

fields.title: Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies
fields.summary: Understanding the technology behind Bitcoin and beyond.
fields.content: Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that records transactions across many computers so that records cannot be altered without consensus of the network. Each block of data is cryptographically linked to the previous block, forming a chain. The blockchain is maintained by a decentralized network of computers (nodes) rather than a central authority like a bank. Bitcoin, created by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto in 2009, was the first cryptocurrency implemented using blockchain technology. Cryptocurrencies are digital or virtual currencies secured by cryptography, making them difficult to counterfeit. Unlike traditional currencies, cryptocurrencies are not issued or controlled by any central bank or government. Mining is the process by which new Bitcoin transactions are verified and added to the blockchain, consuming enormous amounts of electricity. Ethereum extended blockchain technology with smart contracts, self-executing programs that run automatically when conditions are met. DeFi (Decentralized Finance) uses blockchain to create financial services without banks. NFTs (Non-Fungible Tokens) use blockchain to verify ownership of digital assets. Cryptocurrencies are highly volatile and speculative investments. Regulatory environments vary widely between countries. The underlying blockchain technology has applications beyond finance in supply chain, healthcare, voting, and digital identity.

fields.title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
fields.summary: How to understand and protect against cyber threats.
fields.content: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting systems, networks, and programs from digital attacks. As our lives move increasingly online, cybersecurity has become one of the most critical fields in technology. Cyber threats include malware (malicious software designed to harm systems), phishing (deceptive communications that trick people into revealing sensitive information), ransomware (malware that encrypts data and demands payment), social engineering (manipulating people rather than systems), and distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks. The CIA triad is the foundation of information security: Confidentiality (keeping data private), Integrity (ensuring data accuracy), and Availability (ensuring systems are accessible). Encryption converts data into unreadable format that can only be decoded with the correct key. HTTPS on websites indicates encrypted communication. Firewalls monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic. Zero-trust security assumes no user or system is inherently trustworthy and requires continuous verification. The human element is the weakest link in most security systems: social engineering attacks exploit human psychology rather than technical vulnerabilities. Cybersecurity skills are in enormous demand with a global shortage of over 3 million professionals. Certifications like CompTIA Security+, CISSP, and CEH validate cybersecurity expertise.

fields.title: Understanding Cloud Computing
fields.summary: How data and services move to the cloud.
fields.content: Cloud computing delivers computing services including servers, storage, databases, networking, software, and analytics over the internet (the cloud). Instead of owning physical hardware and software, cloud users access these resources as services from cloud providers. The three main service models are Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), where cloud providers offer virtualized computing resources; Platform as a Service (PaaS), which provides a development and deployment environment; and Software as a Service (SaaS), where software is accessed over the internet rather than installed locally. Google Workspace, Microsoft Office 365, Dropbox, and Netflix are everyday SaaS examples. The three major cloud providers are Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. Cloud computing offers businesses advantages including reduced infrastructure costs, automatic scaling to handle demand spikes, global geographic distribution, and access to advanced technologies without expertise. Public clouds share infrastructure among multiple users, private clouds are dedicated to a single organization, and hybrid clouds combine both. Data sovereignty and privacy concerns arise when data is stored in data centers in other countries. The shift to cloud computing has created enormous demand for cloud architects, engineers, and DevOps professionals.

fields.title: Electric Vehicles and the Future
fields.summary: How EVs work and why they are transforming transportation.
fields.content: Electric vehicles (EVs) use electric motors powered by rechargeable battery packs instead of internal combustion engines burning fossil fuels. The electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy with about 90% efficiency, compared to about 30-40% for petrol engines. Lithium-ion batteries store electrical energy, and battery capacity is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh). Range, how far an EV can travel on a full charge, has improved dramatically to 300-600 km for premium vehicles. Charging occurs at home using a wall charger or at public charging stations. Fast chargers can add 200-300 km of range in 20-30 minutes. Regenerative braking recovers energy during braking and converts it back to electricity. EVs produce zero direct emissions, though their overall environmental impact depends on how the electricity is generated. India has ambitious EV adoption targets and the FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles) scheme provides subsidies for EVs. Battery swapping, replacing depleted batteries with charged ones in minutes, is being explored for two and three-wheelers in India. The total cost of ownership of EVs is often lower than comparable petrol vehicles despite higher purchase prices due to lower running costs. Solid-state batteries, expected to arrive in the late 2020s, promise greater energy density, faster charging, and improved safety.

fields.title: Biotechnology and Medicine
fields.summary: How biology and technology are revolutionizing healthcare.
fields.content: Biotechnology applies biological systems and living organisms to develop products and processes for medicine, agriculture, and industry. Modern biotechnology began with the discovery of recombinant DNA technology in 1973, allowing genes from one organism to be inserted into another. Insulin for diabetes treatment was first produced through genetic engineering in 1982, transforming treatment for millions. Monoclonal antibodies are proteins engineered to target specific molecules, used in cancer treatment, autoimmune diseases, and diagnostics. CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, discovered in 2012, allows precise modification of DNA sequences, with potential to correct genetic diseases. CAR-T cell therapy engineers a patient's own immune cells to attack cancer. mRNA vaccines, exemplified by COVID-19 vaccines, deliver genetic instructions for cells to produce a protein that triggers immunity, without using any live pathogen. Pharmacogenomics studies how genetic variation affects drug response, enabling personalized medicine where treatments are tailored to individual genetic profiles. Bioinformatics uses computational tools to analyze biological data, accelerating drug discovery. Synthetic biology designs and builds new biological parts, devices, and systems. Stem cell therapy explores replacing damaged or diseased cells with healthy ones. Bioethics addresses the moral questions raised by biotechnology advances.

fields.title: Quantum Computing
fields.summary: The next frontier in computation and what it means for the future.
fields.content: Quantum computing harnesses quantum mechanical phenomena like superposition and entanglement to perform certain computations exponentially faster than classical computers. Classical computers use bits that are either 0 or 1. Quantum computers use quantum bits (qubits) that can exist in superposition, being both 0 and 1 simultaneously until measured. This allows quantum computers to explore many solutions simultaneously. Entanglement links qubits so the state of one instantly influences another regardless of distance. Quantum computers are not universally faster than classical computers but excel at specific problem types: optimization problems, simulating molecular and chemical systems, and cryptography. Shor's algorithm can break most current encryption by factoring large numbers exponentially faster than any known classical algorithm, threatening current internet security. Grover's algorithm provides a quadratic speedup for searching unsorted databases. Current quantum computers are noisy and error-prone, requiring near-absolute zero temperatures to operate. IBM, Google, and several startups are racing to build practical quantum computers. Google claimed quantum supremacy in 2019 when their 53-qubit processor solved a specific problem in 200 seconds that would take classical computers 10,000 years. Post-quantum cryptography is being developed to secure systems against future quantum attacks. Quantum computing could revolutionize drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, and optimization.

fields.title: General Knowledge Quiz 1
fields.description: Test your general knowledge with these questions!

fields.question_text: What does DNS stand for?
fields.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System. It translates domain names like google.com into IP addresses.

fields.question_text: Which process causes the sky to appear blue?
fields.explanation: Rayleigh Scattering causes blue light to scatter across the sky because blue light has a shorter wavelength.

fields.question_text: What is the main driver of the water cycle?
fields.explanation: The water cycle is primarily driven by solar energy which causes evaporation.

fields.question_text: How many planets are in our solar system?
fields.explanation: There are 8 planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

fields.question_text: What year did the Wright Brothers achieve the first powered flight?
fields.explanation: The Wright Brothers achieved the first powered flight on December 17, 1903 at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

fields.question_text: Approximately how many neurons does the human brain contain?
fields.explanation: The human brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons, each capable of connecting with thousands of others.

fields.question_text: What is the primary cause of current climate change?
fields.explanation: While natural factors affect climate, human activities especially burning fossil fuels have been the dominant cause of climate change since industrialization.

fields.question_text: When was the GPS system fully operational?
fields.explanation: The GPS system became fully operational in 1995, though it was developed by the US Department of Defense starting in the 1970s.

fields.question_text: What is the currency unit GPS accuracy measured in?
fields.explanation: GPS is accurate to about 3-5 meters for civilian use, though military systems achieve much greater precision.

fields.question_text: Where was democracy first practiced in its early form?
fields.explanation: Democracy originated in ancient Athens, Greece around 508 BCE under the statesman Cleisthenes.

fields.question_text: What percentage of the solar system's mass does the Sun contain?
fields.explanation: The Sun contains approximately 99.86% of the solar system's total mass, with Jupiter accounting for most of the rest.

fields.question_text: How long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth?
fields.explanation: Light from the Sun takes approximately 8 minutes to reach Earth, traveling at 299,792 km/s.

fields.question_text: What year was the first permanent photograph taken?
fields.explanation: The first permanent photograph was taken by Joseph Nicephore Niepce in 1826, requiring an 8-hour exposure.

fields.question_text: How many languages are spoken in the world today?
fields.explanation: There are approximately 7,000 languages spoken in the world today, though about 40% are endangered.

fields.question_text: What frequency does the note A above middle C vibrate at?
fields.explanation: The note A above middle C vibrates at exactly 440 Hz, which is the international standard tuning pitch.

fields.question_text: How many glasses of water should you drink daily?
fields.explanation: Health experts recommend drinking at least 8 glasses of water per day to stay properly hydrated.

fields.question_text: What does 2FA stand for in cybersecurity?
fields.explanation: 2FA stands for Two Factor Authentication. It adds an extra security layer beyond just a password.

fields.question_text: What fraction of people experience a mental health problem each year?
fields.explanation: About 1 in 4 people will experience a mental health problem each year, making mental health extremely common.

fields.question_text: What is the 20-20-20 rule for eye health?
fields.option_b: Every 20 min look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds
fields.option_c: Sleep 20 hours, wake 20 hours, repeat 20 days
fields.option_d: Eat 20 grams of vitamins every 20 days for 20 weeks
fields.explanation: The 20-20-20 rule for preventing digital eye strain: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds.

fields.question_text: How many hours of sleep do adults need per night?
fields.explanation: Adults need 7-9 hours of quality sleep per night for optimal health, though individual needs vary slightly.

fields.question_text: In CPR, what is the ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths?
fields.explanation: Standard CPR involves 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths, repeated until help arrives.

fields.question_text: What should you do for a burn injury?
fields.explanation: For burns, run cool (not cold) water over the burn for 20 minutes. Never apply butter or toothpaste.

fields.question_text: What is the normal blood pressure reading?
fields.explanation: Normal blood pressure is below 120/80 mmHg. High blood pressure (hypertension) is defined as 130/80 mmHg or higher.

fields.question_text: What percentage of the immune system is located in the gut?
fields.explanation: Approximately 70% of the immune system is located in the gut, making gut health crucial for overall immunity.

fields.question_text: How long should you wash hands with soap?
fields.explanation: You should wash hands with soap for at least 20 seconds to effectively remove harmful bacteria and viruses.

fields.question_text: What disease was completely eradicated through vaccination?
fields.explanation: Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980, making it the only human disease to have been completely eradicated through vaccination.

fields.question_text: How many minutes of moderate exercise per week does WHO recommend?
fields.explanation: The WHO recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity per week for adults.

fields.question_text: What hormone is primarily released during deep sleep?
fields.explanation: Growth hormone is primarily released during deep sleep, which is essential for tissue repair and children's development.

fields.question_text: What vitamin is primarily obtained from sunlight?
fields.explanation: Vitamin D is primarily synthesized in the skin when exposed to sunlight (UVB rays). It supports bone health and immune function.

fields.question_text: What type of diabetes requires daily insulin injections?
fields.explanation: Type 1 diabetes occurs when the immune system destroys insulin-producing cells, requiring daily insulin injections to survive.

fields.question_text: What does the STAR method stand for in job interviews?
fields.explanation: STAR stands for Situation, Task, Action, Result - a method for answering behavioral interview questions with specific examples.

fields.question_text: What is the 50-30-20 budgeting rule?
fields.explanation: The 50-30-20 rule allocates 50% of income to needs, 30% to wants, and 20% to savings and debt repayment.

fields.question_text: What does BATNA stand for in negotiation?
fields.option_a: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement
fields.explanation: BATNA stands for Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement. Knowing your BATNA gives you power in negotiations.

fields.question_text: What is the Pomodoro Technique?
fields.option_d: Working for 2 hours then taking a 30-minute break
fields.explanation: The Pomodoro Technique involves working in focused 25-minute intervals followed by 5-minute breaks to maintain concentration.

fields.question_text: What percentage of jobs are filled through networking?
fields.explanation: Studies show that up to 80% of jobs are filled through networking rather than advertised positions, making professional relationships crucial.

fields.question_text: What programming language is recommended for beginners due to its readable syntax?
fields.explanation: Python is recommended for beginners due to its clean, readable syntax and versatility in data science, web development, and automation.

fields.question_text: What does SMART stand for in goal setting?
fields.explanation: SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound - a framework for effective goal setting.

fields.question_text: What is the most effective study technique according to research?
fields.explanation: Active recall (testing yourself without looking at notes) is the most powerful learning technique, far more effective than passive re-reading.

fields.question_text: What does SEO stand for in digital marketing?
fields.explanation: SEO stands for Search Engine Optimization - the practice of improving website visibility in search engine results.

fields.question_text: What is Parkinson's Law?
fields.option_a: Work quality improves with time pressure
fields.option_b: Work expands to fill the time available
fields.option_c: Productivity decreases after 8 hours of work
fields.option_d: Teams work better with fewer members
fields.explanation: Parkinson's Law states that work expands to fill the time available for its completion, which is why setting shorter deadlines increases efficiency.

fields.question_text: What is the Feynman Technique for learning?
fields.option_b: Explaining concepts as if teaching a child
fields.explanation: The Feynman Technique involves explaining concepts in simple language as if teaching a child, which reveals gaps in understanding.

fields.question_text: What is emotional intelligence?
fields.option_a: High IQ combined with academic success
fields.option_b: Ability to solve complex emotional problems
fields.option_c: Recognizing and managing your emotions and understanding others'
fields.option_d: Being very sensitive to others' feelings
fields.explanation: Emotional intelligence is the ability to recognize and manage your own emotions while understanding and influencing others' emotions.

fields.question_text: What is the Eisenhower Matrix used for?
fields.option_b: Categorizing tasks by urgency and importance
fields.explanation: The Eisenhower Matrix categorizes tasks into four quadrants by urgency and importance to help prioritize effectively.

fields.question_text: What is mise en place in cooking?
fields.option_d: The final presentation of a dish
fields.explanation: Mise en place is a French term meaning everything in its place, referring to prepping and organizing all ingredients before cooking.

fields.question_text: What does the lean startup approach emphasize?
fields.option_a: Hiring as many people as possible early
fields.option_c: Testing assumptions quickly and cheaply through MVPs
fields.option_d: Waiting until the product is perfect before launching
fields.explanation: The lean startup approach tests assumptions quickly and cheaply through minimum viable products (MVPs) before investing heavily in development.

fields.question_text: What is the most common beginner mistake in drawing?
fields.option_b: Drawing what you think something looks like rather than what you see
fields.explanation: The key breakthrough for beginner artists is learning to draw what you actually see rather than your mental symbol for an object.

fields.question_text: What does origami come from?
fields.option_a: Chinese words for art and paper
fields.option_b: Japanese words for folding and paper
fields.option_c: Korean words for craft and sheet
fields.option_d: Sanskrit words for peace and fold
fields.explanation: Origami comes from Japanese words ori (folding) and kami (paper), the ancient art of paper folding.

fields.question_text: What is the rule of thirds in photography?
fields.option_b: Take three photos of every subject
fields.option_c: Divide the frame into a 3x3 grid and place subjects at intersections
fields.option_d: Use three color tones in every image
fields.explanation: The rule of thirds divides the frame into a 3x3 grid; placing subjects at intersection points creates more dynamic compositions.

fields.question_text: What is the golden hour in photography?
fields.option_a: The most expensive time to hire a photographer
fields.option_b: Shortly after sunrise and before sunset when light is warm and flattering
fields.option_c: Midday when the sun is at its highest
fields.option_d: The first hour after rain stops
fields.explanation: The golden hour, shortly after sunrise and before sunset, provides warm, soft, flattering light ideal for photography.

fields.question_text: According to Japanese legend, folding how many cranes grants a wish?
fields.explanation: According to Japanese legend, folding 1000 paper cranes (senbazuru) grants a wish, symbolizing longevity and good fortune.

fields.question_text: What is the most important seasoning in cooking?
fields.explanation: Salt is the most important seasoning in cooking and should be added at multiple stages throughout the cooking process.

fields.question_text: What is the first essential skill in learning to dance?
fields.explanation: Finding the beat, the steady pulse in music, is the first essential skill in learning to dance.

fields.question_text: What software is recommended for free digital painting?
fields.explanation: Krita is a professional-quality free and open-source digital painting application recommended for beginners and professionals alike.

fields.question_text: What is the primary research-backed benefit of reading fiction?
fields.option_c: Improved theory of mind (understanding others' feelings)
fields.explanation: Research shows that reading fiction improves theory of mind, the ability to understand and attribute mental states to others.

fields.question_text: How long does research suggest mindfulness practice needs to be done before brain changes occur?
fields.explanation: Research shows that 8 weeks of regular mindfulness practice measurably changes brain structure in regions associated with learning and emotional regulation.

fields.question_text: What are valley folds and mountain folds in origami?
fields.option_a: Types of paper used in origami
fields.option_b: The two basic moves from which all origami is constructed
fields.explanation: Valley folds (folding toward you) and mountain folds (folding away from you) are the two fundamental moves in all origami.

fields.question_text: What is the show do not tell principle in creative writing?
fields.option_a: Always use dialogue instead of narration
fields.option_b: Write visual scenes without describing characters' feelings directly
fields.option_c: Show your manuscript to others before submitting
fields.option_d: Use more action and less dialogue
fields.explanation: Show don't tell means conveying emotions and events through specific details and actions rather than directly stating feelings.

fields.question_text: What game is proven to improve academic performance especially in mathematics?
fields.explanation: Chess has been shown to improve academic performance, particularly in mathematics, by developing strategic thinking and pattern recognition.

fields.question_text: What is the three-act structure in storytelling?
fields.explanation: The three-act structure divides stories into Setup (introducing characters and world), Confrontation (conflict and complications), and Resolution.

fields.question_text: What is an open chord in guitar?
fields.option_a: A chord played on the highest strings
fields.option_b: A chord that uses open (unfretted) strings
fields.option_c: A chord with all strings strummed
fields.option_d: The first chord in any progression
fields.explanation: Open chords use at least one open (unfretted) string. Basic open chords like E minor, A minor, D, C, and G allow you to play thousands of songs.

fields.question_text: How many Fundamental Rights does the Indian Constitution guarantee?
fields.explanation: The Indian Constitution guarantees six Fundamental Rights: Equality, Freedom, Against Exploitation, Religion, Cultural/Educational, and Constitutional Remedies.

fields.question_text: How much annual income support does PM-KISAN provide?
fields.explanation: PM-KISAN provides income support of Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 to farmer families.

fields.question_text: What is the RTI application fee for central government departments?
fields.explanation: The fee for filing an RTI application with central government departments is just Rs. 10. BPL applicants are exempt from fees.

fields.question_text: How many days of guaranteed employment does MGNREGA provide annually?
fields.explanation: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage employment per year to rural households whose adult members are willing to do unskilled manual work.

fields.question_text: What fraction of Panchayati Raj seats are reserved for women?
fields.explanation: One-third of seats in Panchayati Raj institutions are reserved for women, and some states have increased this to 50%.

fields.question_text: What is the maximum health insurance cover under PM-JAY per family per year?
fields.explanation: PM-JAY provides health cover of up to Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.

fields.question_text: What is the interest subsidy available to EWS under PMAY-CLSS?
fields.explanation: EWS beneficiaries under PMAY's Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme can receive subsidies up to Rs. 2.67 lakh on home loans up to Rs. 6 lakh.

fields.question_text: What is DigiLocker?
fields.option_a: A physical safe for important documents
fields.option_b: A government cloud platform for storing digital documents
fields.option_c: An app for managing digital payments
fields.option_d: A cybersecurity tool for government employees
fields.explanation: DigiLocker is a government cloud-based platform for citizens to store and share digital documents, reducing the need for physical documents.

fields.question_text: What is the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana?
fields.option_a: A scheme for senior citizen savings
fields.option_b: A savings scheme for girl children with attractive interest rates
fields.option_c: A loan scheme for women entrepreneurs
fields.option_d: A health scheme for pregnant women
fields.explanation: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is a savings scheme for girl children that offers attractive interest rates and tax benefits, encouraging savings for girls' education and marriage.

fields.question_text: What does the Consumer Protection Act 2019 cover?
fields.explanation: The Consumer Protection Act 2019 covers goods, services, and e-commerce, providing comprehensive protection across all types of consumer transactions.

fields.question_text: What constitutional amendment established the Panchayati Raj system?
fields.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment of 1992 mandated the Panchayati Raj system of local self-governance at the village level.

fields.question_text: Under PM-KISAN, how many annual installments are payments made?
fields.explanation: PM-KISAN provides Rs. 6,000 annually in three installments of Rs. 2,000 each, transferred directly to farmers' bank accounts.

fields.question_text: Who can file an RTI application?
fields.explanation: Any Indian citizen can file an RTI application to request information from any public authority covered by the Act.

fields.question_text: What is the purpose of the National Green Tribunal?
fields.option_b: A specialized court for environmental cases
fields.explanation: The National Green Tribunal (NGT), established in 2010, is a specialized judicial body for hearing cases related to environmental protection.

fields.question_text: What does NDRF stand for?
fields.explanation: NDRF stands for National Disaster Response Force, a specialized force trained for disaster rescue and relief operations across India.

fields.question_text: What does AI stand for?
fields.explanation: AI stands for Artificial Intelligence - the ability of machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.

fields.question_text: What was the first artificial satellite launched into space?
fields.explanation: Sputnik, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957, was the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth, marking the beginning of the Space Age.

fields.question_text: What was India's achievement with Chandrayaan-3?
fields.option_c: First to land near the Moon's south pole
fields.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the Moon's south pole in 2023, making India the fourth country to land on the Moon and the first near the pole.

fields.question_text: What is the CIA triad in cybersecurity?
fields.explanation: The CIA triad is the foundation of information security: Confidentiality (keeping data private), Integrity (ensuring accuracy), and Availability (ensuring access).

fields.question_text: What percentage efficiency does an electric motor achieve compared to a petrol engine?
fields.option_a: Electric motors are 50% efficient vs 30-40% for petrol
fields.option_b: Electric motors are 90% efficient vs 30-40% for petrol
fields.option_c: Electric motors are 70% efficient vs 60% for petrol
fields.option_d: Both are equally efficient at about 60%
fields.explanation: Electric motors convert electrical energy to mechanical energy with about 90% efficiency, compared to about 30-40% for internal combustion engines.

fields.question_text: What is the structure of DNA called?
fields.explanation: DNA has a double helix structure, like a twisted ladder, discovered by Watson, Crick, Franklin, and Wilkins in 1953.

fields.question_text: What does IoT stand for?
fields.explanation: IoT stands for Internet of Things - the network of physical devices embedded with sensors and connectivity to collect and exchange data.

fields.question_text: Who created Bitcoin?
fields.explanation: Bitcoin was created by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto in 2009. The true identity of Satoshi Nakamoto remains unknown.

fields.question_text: What are the three main cloud service models?
fields.explanation: The three cloud service models are IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service), PaaS (Platform as a Service), and SaaS (Software as a Service).

fields.question_text: What does mRNA stand for in vaccine technology?
fields.explanation: mRNA stands for Messenger RNA. mRNA vaccines deliver genetic instructions for cells to produce a protein that triggers an immune response.

fields.question_text: What is a qubit in quantum computing?
fields.option_b: A quantum bit that can exist in superposition of 0 and 1
fields.explanation: A qubit (quantum bit) can exist in superposition, being both 0 and 1 simultaneously until measured, unlike classical bits which are only 0 or 1.

fields.question_text: What is CRISPR-Cas9 used for?
fields.explanation: CRISPR-Cas9 is a gene editing technology that allows precise modification of DNA sequences, with potential to correct genetic diseases.

fields.question_text: What does UPI stand for?
fields.explanation: UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface, India's revolutionary real-time digital payment system that has transformed financial transactions.

fields.question_text: What is regenerative braking in electric vehicles?
fields.option_b: Converting braking energy back into electricity
fields.option_c: A faster braking system than conventional brakes
fields.explanation: Regenerative braking recovers energy during braking and converts it back into electricity, stored in the battery to extend range.

fields.question_text: What is the greenhouse effect?
fields.option_b: Greenhouse gases trapping heat in the atmosphere
fields.option_c: The warming effect of green colored surfaces
fields.option_d: Heat generated by factories and cities
fields.explanation: The greenhouse effect occurs when greenhouse gases like CO2 and methane absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit it, keeping Earth warm.
